parts.note: to launch something is to start it off
urns are vessels, jars for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: Celebrities are invited to launch ships at a naming ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits the letters as START URNS; the answer splits them differently, as a phrase for headline performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Headline acts or celebrities on a bill are its main attractions, the performers everyone comes to see.

clue.text: Spaniel does well with little demur

parts.note: a well is a spring, a source of water rising from the ground
er is the small hesitant noise of someone voicing a mild objection

explanation.surface: A dog performs well with only a slight objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' and 'with' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of gun dog, a type of spaniel used to flush game.

clue.text: Giving stylish, spirited account firstly demands precision

indicators.note: firstly says the word for account is placed at the front of the build

parts.note: U means upper-class, hence posh or stylish
racy means lively or spirited

explanation.surface: A lively, stylish report needs to be exact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firstly' looks like a first-letters signal on 'account', but it puts ACC first. U as 'upper-class' is a crossword convention for posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exact and correct is the quality of precision; the two are synonyms.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken or heard, so the word for tense is to be said out loud

parts.note: taut means stretched tight, tense

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be nervous while being given lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUT and the answer are pronounced alike. 'on being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone instructed has been given lessons, the past participle of teach.

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them
her refers to the woman

explanation.surface: It would be better to abandon the lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun (sand) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'I would sooner', it means by preference, more willingly.

definitions.meaning: of a complexion, florid or blood-red
hopeful and optimistic about the future

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both blood-red of face and cheerfully optimistic, from the old humour of blood thought to cause cheerfulness.

clue.text: Stations old Austrian in high school

indicators.note: in tells us the German word is placed inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: alt is German, the language of Austria, for old

explanation.surface: An elderly Austrian is enrolled at a secondary school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a halt is a small railway stopping place with no station buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Small unstaffed railway stops in Britain are called by this name, so they are minor stations.

clue.text: Quite determined not to be saved

definitions.meaning: set on getting one's way whatever happens
read literally, bent on going to hell, so damned and unredeemed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means recklessly resolved, and literally heading for damnation rather than salvation.

clue.text: See superb horse mounted by the porch

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

indicators.note: mounted means raised up, so in a down clue the word for superb is read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: Look at the fine horse being ridden by the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' suggests a rider but turns A1 upwards, giving IA. 'by the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-sided gallery or covered veranda attached to a house is a kind of porch.

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: That kind of thing suits a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name but is a military dash out from a besieged position.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attack by troops from a defended position, the same as a raid out.

definitions.meaning: count a second time, as with votes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means narrating a story, and also counting votes a second time, the old sense of tell as count.

parts.note: high means tall
light describes fair, blonde hair

explanation.surface: A tall fair-haired woman turns heads.
explanation.walkthrough: A blonde streak in hair is also a highlight, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise something is to make it stand out, so drawing focus to it.

clue.text: Greek later became a hard worker

parts.note: after means later

explanation.surface: A Greek man eventually turned into a diligent labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for someone who toils diligently; graft is hard work.

clue.text: Furious about Lawrence having to recap

indicators.note: about means around, so the angry word goes round the initials

parts.note: irate means furious
T E Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials

explanation.surface: An angry man is cross with Lawrence and must summarise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat or restate is to go over again, which is what recapping does.

clue.text: Hear all-Tory ball is set for London venue

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A dance attended only by Conservatives is scheduled for a London concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous concert hall in Kensington, home of the Proms, a celebrated London venue.

clue.text: Insouciant trainee needs succour and support

parts.note: L stands for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
aid means succour or help
to back is to support

explanation.surface: An unworried apprentice wants help and backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and easy-going describes someone carefree, unconcerned, insouciant.

parts.note: left means went away
over means finished

explanation.surface: Someone departed and completed whatever was still to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or material still there after the rest is used is a remnant.

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the male pronoun
unusually tells us the letters of ardent are arranged in a different way

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: An unusually passionate man is a devoted follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' makes ADRENT from ARDENT; 'about' puts it round HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or leader is a disciple.

clue.text: Odd piles set at an angle

indicators.note: set means arranged or placed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange heaps are placed crookedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven and leaning to one side means askew, at an angle.

parts.note: de is French for from
brief is slang for a barrister or lawyer

explanation.surface: Collect news from a French lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like part of the definition but joins 'French' to give DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone after a mission is to extract a report or information from them.

clue.text: Master turning up with society girl? Rubbish!

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word for master is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sir is a title of address for a master

explanation.surface: A master appears with a debutante, and someone exclaims in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes RIS from SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered fragments or waste left behind is refuse, or rubbish.

indicators.note: headed asks for the head, the first letter, of the word big

parts.note: an ounce is a tiny weight

explanation.surface: A conceited featherweight is full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bigheaded' looks like conceited but splits as 'Big headed', giving B.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and energy, as in a spring in one's step, is vitality.

clue.text: Learn again how to make a beehive?

definitions.meaning: to revise or refresh a skill
a beehive is a tall hairdo, which is made by combing the hair upwards

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means revise a subject, and literally sweeping hair upward into a tall beehive hairdo.

clue.text: Move on time to allocate resources

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

explanation.surface: Moving on in time to share out the funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning spending means deciding how money will be allocated.

clue.text: Peter supports peace-keepers, but it's risky

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means the word for Peter sits below the other piece

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, provides peacekeeping forces
peter is underworld slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A man called Peter backs the peace-keepers, though it is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name but is criminal slang for a strongbox. 'but it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous or hazardous means not secure, so it is risky.

parts.note: blue means sad or despondent
a blood is an old word for a fashionable young man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A gloomy fop shows aristocratic breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displays' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocratic descent, and the people of it, are the nobility.

definitions.meaning: permission, as in being given leave to start

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means proceed or progress; as a noun it means permission to begin.

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Dot kisses a Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name. 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spot or mark is a dot.

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
if you treated someone you paid for them

explanation.surface: Former soldiers paid for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a description of the servicemen but means withdrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire from a position is to withdraw or fall back from it.
